$comment: Chain claims-sibling convention as in del-mh-001. The chain_hash here is a literal wrong value (43 'A' chars), NOT a placeholder: the minter signs the outer token over these claims as-is, so the outer JWS signature is VALID over the wrong chain_hash — the recomputation check (RFC-AITP-0011 §5) is the isolated failure.
description: Multi-hop chain_hash truncation defense (aitp/0.3 shape). The chain is identical to del-mh-001 — every hop's JWS and the voucher inside chain[0] verify, continuity, expiry, and scope all pass — but the outer token's `chain_hash` claim does not match the recomputed digest-array commitment base64url(sha256(JCS([d_0]))) where d_0 = base64url(sha256(ASCII(chain[0])))). The verifier MUST recompute chain_hash from the received chain array and reject on mismatch with DELEGATION_CHAIN_HASH_MISMATCH (RFC-AITP-0011 §5). This models a final delegator committing to a different chain than it carries (equivalent in effect to truncation or substitution). Note: unlike the v0.1-era vector, the outer signature is VALID here — the wrong chain_hash is bound under C's signature at mint time — so the recomputation step, not signature verification, is what fails. The reference recomputation is pinned at kat-multihop-truncation-001 (re-specified for aitp/0.3 digest-array form). Manifest source: `input.issuer_manifests` carries the signed Manifests of both hop issuers, B (kat-keypair-002, chain[0].iss) and C (kat-keypair-003, outer iss); each hop's JWS verifies under the key its issuer's Manifest designates (RFC-AITP-0011 §3 step 1). The voucher needs no Manifest: A verifies it under its own key.

expected.rationale: The chain_hash claim is all-'A's, which cannot equal the digest-array commitment recomputed from the carried chain (RFC-AITP-0011 §5 step 2). The outer signature is valid over the claims as minted, so the failure isolates the recomputation check; rejection also covers the equivalent truncation case, since dropping or substituting a hop changes the recomputed value the same way.
